pitch_detail.notes: Talus/snow from Crescent Creek Basin to the base of the summit horn.
Slabs and ledges gaining the ridge below the summit tower; route-finding is ambiguous and it's easy to traverse too low.
Short low-5th-class wall/step to the summit ridge; usually roped.
Exposed scramble along the ridge to the true summit.

climbing_route.label: Choss slope to the notch south of the summit
climbing_route.notes: From the snowfield and small glacier remnant below the peak's south side, claw up dirt and broken rock to the notch immediately south of Degenhardt — the same notch that forms the upper crossing point of the Barrier. This is the worst rock on the route and is consistently described as marking the end of any good climbing in the area. Everything here is loose enough that a party should stay tight and out of each other's fall line, and running meltwater over the slabby sections has been reported as a slip hazard.

climbing_route.label: South ridge to the summit tower
climbing_route.notes: From the notch, follow the ridge north toward the summit over exposed but moderate ground. Route-finding matters more than difficulty: parties report traversing much too low and having to regain height. A small tower guards the final notch and is turned rather than climbed direct.

climbing_route.label: Summit blocks
climbing_route.notes: The last moves onto the 8,000-plus ft summit are short 4th class on poor rock, with some parties describing the finish as low fifth depending on the line taken. A rappel anchor has been noted on the south side, though the section is commonly downclimbed. Degenhardt is widely regarded as the chossiest peak in the Southern Pickets, so helmets and careful rope management on the descent matter more than the grade suggests.

wa_mount_degenhardt_southwest_route.beta: Approach from Goodell Creek Trail, crossing Terror Creek to reach the ridge system. Traverse through Crescent Creek Basin under the southwest slope, then ascend to the summit horn. The route involves mixed snow and rock terrain, with technical climbing concentrated on the summit block.
wa_mount_degenhardt_southwest_route.approach: Start at the Goodell Creek Trailhead (Goodell Creek Group Camp, ~500-600 ft) off SR-20 just west of Newhalem. The first stretch follows an old logging-road grade/climbers' path along Goodell Creek for a little over a mile before it narrows to a boot-beaten track. Roughly 4 miles in, near Terror Creek, watch for the unmarked junction where the Terror Creek climbers' path splits off — historically flagged only by a rock arrow, a post, and a large cairn, so route-finding here is a genuine crux; the path is well-defined at first but dies out into creek-bottom brush and devils club lower down. Ford/cross Terror Creek at about 2000 ft: the customary crossing is a large log roughly 500 ft upstream of where the path hits the creek, but in high water this log is sometimes submerged and parties have had to scout alternate logs — treat this as a conditions-dependent obstacle, not a given. From the creek, the path grinds directly and relentlessly up the opposing hillside, gaining close to 4000 ft in under two miles through forest, then open heather slopes above treeline — steep, loose in spots, and a reported source of overuse injuries (at least one climber has torn a calf muscle here). The climbers' path eventually merges into 'Stump Hollow' and follows the narrow crest north to the standard basecamp area near 'Chopping Block Camp' (~6000-6400 ft), the usual base for Southern Pickets objectives. From camp, the approach to Degenhardt itself continues: traverse Stump Hollow to the roughly 6400 ft saddle near the Chopping Block, then descend about 200 ft into Crescent Creek Basin. This is where you make the Barrier crossing — the long rocky rib dividing Terror Basin from Crescent Creek Basin. There are two options: a lower crossing over loose ledges at the base of the Terror Glacier, or a higher crossing over moats and steep choss near the top of the glacier just below Degenhardt (the preferred option if camped near Terror Basin and climbing Degenhardt, Pyramid, or Terror); both are loose, exposed, and consistently described as 'Pickets Class 3' — sustained, serious, low-fifth-class-feeling terrain despite the modest rating. Beyond the Barrier, cross a snowfield/small glacier below Degenhardt's south side (crampons and an axe are standard gear here even in summer) to reach the base of the southwest line. Total trip is roughly 18.7 miles round-trip with about 600-8100+ ft of elevation range; water is available at Goodell Creek and the Terror Creek crossing, with seasonal snowmelt/tarns higher up that can dry out late season.
wa_mount_degenhardt_southwest_route.descent_text: Reverse the ascent: downclimb the corkscrew line (class 3-4 ledges and a short class 4-5 step) back to the notch below the true summit and onto the Barrier crest. The one consistently reported technical spot is the final summit tower/notch just below the top — most parties either carefully downclimb this class 4/5 step or rig a single short rappel (roughly 30-40 ft) off a sling/tat anchor wrapped around a rock horn or block on the south side; the anchor is natural (no bolts — this is Park wilderness), and the existing tat is often old and weathered, so back it up or replace it if you have spare cord. A single 30m rope (or a 60m used doubled) is more than sufficient for this one rappel — no multi-pitch rappel sequence is needed. Strong parties in good conditions have downclimbed this section without using the rope at all. From there, continue reversing the corkscrew terrain down to the base of the southwest side, re-cross the snowfield/small glacier below (crampons still recommended), climb back up roughly 200 ft to the 6400 ft saddle, and traverse back through Crescent Creek Basin and Stump Hollow to camp — summit-to-camp typically takes roughly 3.5-4 hours. The Barrier crossing is again the main hazard on this leg: loose rock and exposed ledges/choss, more dangerous late in the day when fatigued or in poor light. The next day, reverse the full approach — steep descent off the ridge/Stump Hollow crest to the Terror Creek crossing (re-check the log crossing, since water levels and log position can change), then the climbers' path and Goodell Creek Trail back to the trailhead.
